html:
SMTO-PRX-0002 — Proxmox reported an error for this request

GUID: 1e6bc85c-5704-44ab-9663-71025137abe0
Slug: proxmox-api-error
Domain: PRX · Subsystem: prx

What happened

  • SMTO sent your request to the Proxmox server, but it came back as failed. The exact reason is in the technical details.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Technical details in this panel to see Proxmox's own message. Proxmox's message usually names the problem, such as an unknown machine or a locked VM.
  2. Check that the node name and machine ID you gave SMTO match what the Proxmox web interface shows. A wrong name or ID is a common cause of this error.
  3. If you asked for a change, check in the Proxmox web interface whether it already happened. A failed reply doesn't always mean nothing changed on the server.
  4. Once the problem is fixed and you know the current state, ask SMTO to try the request again. The request can safely run again once its cause is fixed and you know it won't repeat a change.

What success looks like

  • SMTO completes the Proxmox request and reports the result without an error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages your Proxmox server. Don't turn off certificate checks or delete the saved server details to make it work; they aren't the cause of this error.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Proxmox API request failed with a non-success HTTP status or Gateway error that is not a TLS, authentication, session-expiry, permission or unreachable failure, or the Gateway rejected the request before dispatch.

What this means

  • The HTTP result has a failure kind or non-success status and falls through the client's more specific TLS/auth/permission/unreachable mappings. Proxmox task and resource receipts own effect truth. A failed read, expired local wait or invalid response does not undo a mutation; diagnostics never replay writes or escalate graceful shutdown to forced stop.

Why this can happen

  • The HTTP result has a failure kind or non-success status and falls through the client's more specific TLS/auth/permission/unreachable mappings.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect HTTP status, bounded body and resource_executed rather than assuming a connection or input problem.

How to fix it

  • Inspect http_status, details and the Proxmox task log for the node to find the cause, such as a wrong node or VMID, an invalid parameter, a locked guest or a server-side error. Correct it, and for a write confirm the guest's current state before repeating it.
  • Inspect the recorded API status and task log; correct the specific target or service failure.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The original task/effect state is known and the specific API failure is resolved.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.

Technical notes

  • Proxmox task and resource receipts own effect truth. A failed read, expired local wait or invalid response does not undo a mutation; diagnostics never replay writes or escalate graceful shutdown to forced stop.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
